questions.q: Who sat opposite Fogg and Passepartout in the train carriage?
choices: Fix, the detective
Sir Francis Cromarty
The Rev. Decimus Smith
The British consul at Suez
questions.evidence: This was Sir Francis Cromarty, one of Mr. Fogg's whist partners on the Mongolia

questions.q: Where was Sir Francis Cromarty travelling to?
choices: Calcutta, to sail home to England
Benares, to join his corps
Allahabad, to visit his family
Bombay, to meet the governor
questions.evidence: now on his way to join his corps at Benares

questions.q: The narrator says Fogg "was not travelling, but only describing a circumference." What does this mean?
choices: He was drawing careful maps of every country he passed
He was only going around the globe, not learning about the places
He was measuring the exact size of the earth for a learned society
He was travelling in circles because he had lost his way
questions.evidence: who was not travelling, but only describing a circumference, took no pains to inquire into these subjects

questions.q: What did Sir Francis wonder about Fogg?
choices: Whether a human heart really beat beneath his cold exterior
Whether he had ever served as a soldier in the English army
Whether he was secretly the thief who robbed the Bank
Whether he could be beaten at a game of whist
questions.evidence: whether a human heart really beat beneath this cold exterior

questions.q: What delay did Sir Francis say Fogg would have met at the mountains some years before?
choices: The trains used to wait a full day for the mail
Passengers had to cross on ponies or in palanquins
The line was often blocked by deep snow in winter
Travellers needed special passes to enter the hills
questions.evidence: which the passengers were obliged to cross in palanquins or on ponies to Kandallah

questions.q: Why did Fogg say Passepartout's trouble at the pagoda could not have delayed him?
choices: He had already paid the priests for the lost shoes
Passepartout would be punished and go home, and Fogg would go on
Sir Francis would surely speak to the Government on their behalf
The priests did not know which train they had taken
questions.evidence: I don't see how this affair could have delayed his master.

questions.q: What did Passepartout buy at Burhampoor?
choices: A new silver watch
Indian slippers decorated with false pearls
A straw hat to keep off the sun
A blanket to wrap his feet in on the long train ride
questions.evidence: Indian slippers, ornamented with false pearls

questions.q: How had Passepartout's feelings about the journey changed by this point?
choices: He now believed in the bet and worried about any delay
He was now sure that the journey would end in Calcutta
He was now tired of travelling and wanted to go home
He now thought his master was the bank robber after all
questions.evidence: He came to regard his master's project as intended in good earnest, believed in the reality of the bet

questions.q: What did Passepartout blame Fogg for not doing on the train?
choices: Buying first-class tickets
Bribing the engineer
Sending a telegram ahead
Hiring a faster special train
questions.evidence: mentally blaming Mr. Fogg for not having bribed the engineer

questions.q: Why was Passepartout's watch now at least four hours slow?
choices: It had been damaged in the fight at the pagoda
It still showed London time as they went east
He had forgotten to wind it since leaving Suez
Sir Francis had set it wrong as a joke
questions.evidence: always regulated on the Greenwich meridian, which was now some seventy-seven degrees westward

questions.q: Why did the train stop at the hamlet of Kholby?
choices: The engine had run out of English coal
The railway was not finished to Allahabad
A herd of elephants was blocking the track
The bridge over the river had been washed away

questions.q: How many miles of track were still missing between Kholby and Allahabad?
choices: Five
Fifty
Fifteen
Five hundred
questions.evidence: There's still a matter of fifty miles to be laid from here to Allahabad

questions.q: Why wasn't Fogg upset when he learned the railway stopped at Kholby?
choices: He had read about the gap in the newspapers in London
He had expected some obstacle and had two days to spare
He planned to complain to the company and get his money back
He knew Sir Francis could order a special train for them
questions.evidence: I have two days, which I have already gained, to sacrifice.

questions.q: The newspapers "had been premature in their announcement" that the line was complete. What does premature mean here?
choices: Too early
Too angry
Too long
Too quiet
questions.evidence: had been premature in their announcement of the completion of the line

questions.q: What did Fogg say he would do after searching the village and finding no vehicle?
choices: Wait at Kholby for the line to be finished
Go back to Bombay and take a steamer
Go on foot
Ride with the other passengers in a waggon

questions.q: What was the name of the elephant Passepartout found?
choices: Kiouni
Kholby
Kandallah
Kali
questions.evidence: Kiouni--this was the name of the beast

questions.q: How did Fogg finally get the elephant?
choices: He hired it for forty pounds an hour
He bought it outright for two thousand pounds
He traded his carpet-bag and silver watch for it
Sir Francis ordered the owner to lend it
questions.evidence: At two thousand pounds the Indian yielded.

questions.q: Why was Fogg willing to pay so much for the elephant?
choices: He planned to sell it again for more money in Calcutta
He wanted to give it as a gift to his friend Sir Francis Cromarty
It was absolutely necessary to him with the bet at stake
He had always wanted to own an elephant of his own
questions.evidence: the elephant was absolutely necessary to him

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A gap in the railway forces Fogg to buy an elephant to keep going
Passepartout is arrested for his trouble at the pagoda in Bombay
Fogg and Sir Francis play whist all the way across India
Fix finally catches up with Fogg on the train to Calcutta
questions.evidence: in default of any other means of conveyance, Mr. Fogg resolved to hire him
